title: How many multiples of nine lie between 4300 and 4400?
description: The remainders of four thousand three hundred and four thousand four hundred on division by nine give the first and last multiples of nine between them. The video then counts the steps of nine from the first to the last.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the first and last multiples of nine from the remainders, then count the steps of nine between them and add one. Watch for students who count the steps and forget that the number of multiples is one more.

source: Figure it Out (multiples of nine, question 4)
video_script.why: The student can find a remainder on division by nine from the digit sum and now uses the remainders of the two ends to find the first and last multiples between them.
video_script.substitution: Find the remainder of each end from its digit sum, step to the first multiple above the lower end and the last below the upper end, then count the steps of nine.
video_script.anchor: a number strip from 4300 to 4400 with the multiples of nine marked
video_script.payoff_line: There are eleven multiples of nine between them

final_answer.spoken: eleven multiples of nine, from four thousand three hundred two to four thousand three hundred ninety two

maths_rules: 4300 has digit sum 4 + 3 = 7, so it leaves remainder 7; the first multiple of 9 after it is 4300 + 2 = 4302
4400 has digit sum 4 + 4 = 8, so it leaves remainder 8; the last multiple of 9 before it is 4400 - 8 = 4392
4392 - 4302 = 90 = 10 x 9, so there are 10 steps of 9 and 11 multiples
check 4302 = 9 x 478 and 4392 = 9 x 488; the numbers 478 to 488 are 11 numbers
